history.title: A reconstructed history
history.caveat: No source tells this life: every particular of it is ours.
paragraphs: His family is put with the village at the portage, at the camping place of Chicago, three leagues from the fort (about thirty men, Co-wa-bee-mai their chief in May 1812), one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring.
He is of the Bear gens (M′-ko′), and his children are of it after him.
He has a pony, and some winters went as far as the Wabash to hunt.
He came in when the bands gathered at Chicago in August, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets when the goods were handed out.

Ottawonce made his mark on the treaty of St. Louis, 24 August 1816, by which the bands of the Illinois and Milwaukee rivers ceded the land about Chicago: the one record of him we have. Everything else here is reconstructed.

paragraphs: His family is put with the village at the portage, at the camping place of Chicago, three leagues from the fort (about thirty men, Co-wa-bee-mai their chief in May 1812), one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring.

He has seen the French and the English traders come and go, and the Americans build the fort in 1803.
He came in when the bands gathered at Chicago in August, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets when the goods were handed out.
